title: From operating profit to operating cash flow
caption: Profit is not cash. Depreciation is added back because no cash left; money tied up in receivables and inventory is deducted; the rise in payables is added. Here the adjustments cancel out, so operating cash flow equals operating profit: £80,000.
alt: Waterfall from operating profit £80,000: add depreciation £20,000, deduct receivables rise £15,000, add payables rise £5,000, deduct inventory rise £10,000, leaving operating cash flow £80,000.
description: Operating profit £80,000; add depreciation £20,000 to get £100,000.
Inventory rose £10,000: deduct, leaving operating cash flow of £80,000.

relations.name: after receivables the running total is £85,000
